mainTopic: When rain is mentioned and requested: שאלה vs. הזכרה, רבי יהודה's two traditions, the start date in ארץ ישראל, and the practice with two days of יום טוב
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question: does the משנה follow only רבי יהושע? רבא answers that it can follow רבי אליעזר too, because שאלה (requesting rain) and הזכרה (mentioning rain) are separate. Next, a ברייתא seems to contradict רבי יהודה in the משנה about when rain stops at פסח. רב חסדא answers with the same שאלה/הזכרה split, but עולא rejects it and says two תנאים reported רבי יהודה differently. רב יוסף and רבה each try to reread 'until פסח passes' so the sources agree, but both readings fall, and the גמרא concludes 'it is clear, as עולא said.' רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יהודה, and רבי זירא challenges this from רבי אלעזר, who rules like רבן גמליאל (7th of מרחשון). After several attempts, the גמרא settles that both rulings are for ארץ ישראל: the 7th of מרחשון when the בית המקדש stands, and right after סוכות when it does not. Finally, רב and שמואל disagree about when people with two days of יום טוב start mentioning rain. They differ only about מנחה of the first day.

steps.title: Does the משנה follow רבי יהושע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה matches רבי יהושע, who starts the rain prayers from the time the לולב is put down, and not רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the משנה is רבי יהושע, who said we start from the time the לולב is put down?!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a suggestion that the משנה follows only רבי יהושע. If that were true, the משנה would disagree with רבי אליעזר, who starts earlier, from when the לולב is first taken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר starts mentioning rain on the first day of סוכות, when the לולב is taken. רבי יהושע starts only on the last day (שמיני עצרת), when the לולב is put down. The משנה's rule that rain is requested only close to the rainy season seems to match רבי יהושע's later start, which would leave רבי אליעזר out.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who starts mentioning rain from שמיני עצרת
From the time of putting it (the לולב) down, i.e., the end of סוכות

phrases.english: Is it Rabbi Yehoshua,
phrases.notes: This is the tail of the question 'Shall we say our משנה is…'

phrases.english: who said: from the time of putting it (the lulav) down?!
phrases.notes: That is, from שמיני עצרת

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא, דְּאָמַר מִשְּׁעַת הַנָּחָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the previous discussion on the daf, which compared רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה can only be explained according to רבי יהושע, leaving it in conflict with רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבא: requesting and mentioning are separate
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה can even follow רבי אליעזר, because שאלה (requesting rain) and הזכרה (mentioning rain) are two different things.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say it follows רבי אליעזר. Requesting is one thing, and mentioning is another.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The משנה does not have to follow only רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's early start (the first day of סוכות) applies only to הזכרה, meaning praising God as the One who brings rain. The משנה's rule that we request rain only close to the rainy season applies to שאלה, the actual request for rain. Since the two rulings are about different parts of the prayer, they do not conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say
Requesting rain (ותן טל ומטר in ברכת השנים)
Mentioning rain (משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם in גבורות)
Separate, by itself

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two terms. הזכרה is the praise 'משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם' in the second ברכה. שאלה is the actual request 'ותן טל ומטר' in ברכת השנים. They can start and stop at different times.
steps.whyThisMatters: This distinction between שאלה and הזכרה is the key tool of the whole סוגיא. It is used again right away to solve the next contradiction.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even if you say it is Rabbi Eliezer —
requesting is separate, and mentioning is separate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion of step 1 by distinguishing two kinds of rain prayer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה can follow רבי אליעזר, because his ruling concerns הזכרה while the משנה's concerns שאלה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two separate concepts (שאלה vs. הזכרה)

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהודה from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's ruling from the משנה about the prayer leader, including the rule that mentioning rain stops on the first day of פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: The one who passes before the ark, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This is a setup line: the גמרא is preparing to challenge it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the full משנה, רבי יהודה says that on the last day of סוכות, the מוסף leader mentions rain and the שחרית leader does not. On the first day of פסח it is the reverse: the שחרית leader mentions rain and the מוסף leader does not. This means that for רבי יהודה, rain stops being mentioned on the first day of פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose view is being examined
The one who passes before the ark, i.e., the חזן or prayer leader
Etc.: the rest of the משנה is assumed

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The one who passes before the ark, etc.
phrases.notes: Refers to the full משנה: on the first day of פסח the שחרית leader mentions rain and the מוסף leader does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הָעוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the סוגיא by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, mentioning rain stops during the first day of פסח (from מוסף onward).

steps.title: A ברייתא says רבי יהודה continues until after פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says we request rain until פסח has passed, which seems to contradict the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contrasted it: Until when do we request rain? רבי יהודה says: Until פסח has passed. רבי מאיר says: Until ניסן has passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a contradiction. In the ברייתא, רבי יהודה continues the rain prayers through all of פסח, but in the משנה they stop on the first day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same תנא, רבי יהודה, seems to give two different end points: the first day of פסח in the משנה, and the end of פסח in the ברייתא. The other opinion in the ברייתא, רבי מאיר, goes even further, until the end of ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction: introduces a source that conflicts with the one just quoted
Until when
We request
The תנא who holds until the end of ניסן

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
Until when does one request rain?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹר הַפֶּסַח,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Until Passover has passed.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹר נִיסָן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: Until Nisan has passed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבי יהודה ruling quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה that rain stops on the first day of פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא records רבי יהודה saying rain continues until פסח has passed. The same תנא cannot hold two different end points.

steps.title: רב חסדא: one source is about requesting, the other about mentioning
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא resolves the contradiction: the ברייתא is about שאלה, which continues through פסח, and the משנה is about הזכרה, which stops on the first day of פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is not difficult. Here it is about requesting, there it is about mentioning. Requesting continues on; mentioning stops on the first day of the holiday.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the contradiction. The two sources are talking about different parts of the prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבא in step 2, רב חסדא separates שאלה from הזכרה. For רבי יהודה, the request for rain (ותן טל ומטר) keeps going until פסח is over. The mention of rain (משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם) stops already on the first day of פסח. So the משנה and the ברייתא agree.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who resolves the contradiction
It is not difficult: introduces a resolution
Here... there: assigns each source to a different case
Keeps on requesting
Stops

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's answer is that for רבי יהודה, שאלה continues until the end of פסח while הזכרה stops on the first day. Hold this answer loosely: עולא rejects it in the next step, and the גמרא ends up following עולא (steps 12 and 15).

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: It is not difficult:
Here it is about requesting, there it is about mentioning.
To request — one keeps on requesting,
to mention — on the first festival day he stops.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן לִשְׁאוֹל, כָּאן לְהַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 4, using the same principle רבא gave in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different subject (שאלה vs. הזכרה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and the משנה both refer to the same rain prayer, so רבי יהודה contradicts himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to שאלה (until the end of פסח) and the משנה refers to הזכרה (stops on the first day of פסח), so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: עולא Rejects רב חסדא's Answer
steps.stepSummary: עולא says רב חסדא's answer is very hard to accept. If we mention rain even at the start of the season, before we ask for it, then during the days we ask for rain we should certainly mention it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: What רב חסדא said is as hard to take as vinegar on the teeth and smoke in the eyes. Think about it: at a time when we do not ask for rain, we still mention it. So at a time when we do ask for rain, isn't it obvious that we should mention it too?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא attacks רב חסדא's answer from Step 5. He argues that it creates an impossible situation: asking for rain without mentioning it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the start of the rainy season, we begin mentioning rain before we begin asking for it, so mentioning is the 'lighter', earlier stage. רב חסדא's answer creates the reverse situation: during the rest of פסח we would be asking for rain without mentioning it. עולא uses a קל וחומר to show that this makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Difficult, hard to accept
Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes (a verse from משלי, meaning 'very unpleasant')
'Now if…', the opening of a קל וחומר argument
Isn't it logical? (the conclusion of a קל וחומר)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two prayers. מזכיר means mentioning rain ('משיב הרוח') in the second blessing. שואל means asking for rain ('ותן טל ומטר') in the ninth blessing. עולא's point is that mentioning always comes along with asking, so asking without mentioning is backwards.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
That which Rav Chisda said is difficult,
like vinegar to the teeth,
and like smoke to the eyes.
phrases.notes: Quoting משלי 10:26.

phrases.english: Now if, where one does not request rain, one still mentions it,
phrases.notes: For example, at the start of the rainy season.

phrases.english: then where one does request rain,
phrases.notes: For example, during the rest of פסח, according to רב חסדא.

phrases.english: isn't it logical that one should mention it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא קַשְׁיָא כַּחֹמֶץ לַשִּׁנַּיִם וְכֶעָשָׁן לָעֵינָיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer רב חסדא gave in Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's split between שאלה (continuing through פסח) and הזכרה (stopping on the first day)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: mentioning rain happens even without asking, so asking for rain without mentioning it is illogical.

steps.title: עולא's Answer: Two תנאים Disagree About רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: עולא offers a different answer. The משנה and the ברייתא reflect two different תנאים who report רבי יהודה's opinion differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, עולא said: There are two תנאים who disagree about what רבי יהודה held.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רב חסדא's answer, עולא gives his own way to resolve the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of trying to make both sources agree, עולא says they simply do not agree. One תנא reports that רבי יהודה stops both mentioning and asking on the first day of פסח. The other reports that רבי יהודה continues both until the end of פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (signals rejecting the previous approach and offering a new one)
Two תנאים (two different teachers transmitting the opinion)
According to the view of

steps.whyThisMatters: 'Two תנאים according to one sage' is a common last-resort tool in the גמרא. It accepts that the sources really contradict each other, because different students remembered the teacher's view differently.

phrases.english: Rather, Ulla said:
It is a dispute between two tannaim regarding the view of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר עוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב חסדא's rejected answer with a new resolution
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two תנאים disagree about the view of one sage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources report the same view of רבי יהודה, so they must be reconciled
steps.terutzMaskana: The sources reflect two different traditions of רבי יהודה's view

steps.title: רב יוסף Reinterprets 'Until פסח Passes'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reads the ברייתא's phrase 'until פסח passes' to mean 'until the first prayer leader of the first day of פסח finishes.' This makes the ברייתא match the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What does 'until פסח passes' mean? It means until the first שליח ציבור who goes down to lead the prayers on the first day of יום טוב of פסח has passed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a third way to resolve the contradiction. He reinterprets a word in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יעבור' (passes) is read as the prayer leader 'passing' before the ark, not as the whole holiday of פסח ending. With this reading, the ברייתא and the משנה give the same cutoff time, so there is no contradiction at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of (introduces a reinterpretation)
Until it passes
The prayer leader
Who goes down (to lead the prayers before the ark)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
What does 'until Passover has passed' mean?
Until the first prayer leader has passed
phrases.notes: Passed before the ark, meaning he finished leading the prayer.

phrases.aramaic: הַיּוֹרֵד בְּיוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח.
phrases.english: who goes down to lead on the first Festival day of Passover.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר מַאי עַד שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹר הַפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another, separate resolution of the contradiction from Step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Until פסח passes' means until the whole holiday is over
steps.terutzMaskana: It means until the first prayer leader of the first day of פסח finishes, the same cutoff as in the משנה

steps.title: אביי: There Is No Request for Rain on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף. On יום טוב we do not ask for rain at all, so how could the ברייתא say we ask for rain until the prayer of the first day of פסח?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is there any asking for rain on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's reading. On יום טוב, the עמידה does not include the blessing where we ask for rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking for rain is part of ברכת השנים, the ninth blessing of the weekday עמידה, and that blessing is not said on יום טוב. Under רב יוסף's reading, the ברייתא would be telling us to keep asking for rain right through the first day of יום טוב. That is impossible, because there is no asking on that day at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him (introduces a direct challenge)
Is there? (a rhetorical 'there isn't!')
The ninth blessing of the weekday עמידה, where rain is requested

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Is there a request for rain on a Festival?
phrases.notes: The weekday blessings, including ברכת השנים, are not said on יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי שְׁאֵלָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב מִי אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's reinterpretation in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reading that the ברייתא's cutoff for שאלה is the first day of פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On יום טוב there is no שאלה at all, so the ברייתא could not be describing asking for rain up to the prayer of the first day of יום טוב.

steps.title: רב יוסף says the translator asks for rain
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers אביי: yes, the ברייתא means the first day of פסח, but the asking for rain is done by the מתורגמן, not in the עמידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, the translator asks for rain.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends himself against אביי's question. He says the 'asking' on the first day of פסח is not part of the יום טוב prayer. It is a request said out loud by the מתורגמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי asked how anyone could ask for rain on יום טוב, since the יום טוב תפילה has no request for rain. רב יוסף agrees that the תפילה has no such request. He moves the 'asking' to someone else: the מתורגמן, who speaks to the community. That way the ברייתא can still say rain is asked for until the first day of פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes (Aramaic)
The translator or announcer who passed the teacher's or reader's words on to the community
Asks or requests (here: asks for rain)

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב יוסף answering אביי

phrases.english: Yes, the translator requests (rain).
phrases.notes: Not in the עמידה, but a request announced to the community

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין שׁוֹאֵל מְתוּרְגְּמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines who does the 'asking': the מתורגמן, not the person praying
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'asking' must mean the request inside the עמידה, which does not exist on יום טוב
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'asking' on the first day of פסח is done by the מתורגמן

steps.title: Would a translator ask for something the community doesn't need?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב יוסף's answer: a מתורגמן would never ask for something the community does not need, and rain is not needed at פסח time.
steps.simpleTranslation: But would a translator ask for something the community does not need?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By פסח the rainy season is over, and rain is no longer wanted. So it makes no sense for a מתורגמן to ask for rain in front of everyone at that time. Moving the request to the מתורגמן does not fix the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: But would...? (introduces a doubtful, challenging question)
The community or congregation

phrases.english: But would a translator request
phrases.notes: A question that is really a rejection

phrases.english: something the community does not need?
phrases.notes: Rain at פסח is not needed

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מְתוּרְגְּמָן שׁוֹאֵל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לַצִּבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's answer from Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the מתורגמן asks for rain on the first day of פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nobody publicly asks for something the community does not want, and rain at פסח is not wanted

steps.title: So it must be like עולא
steps.stepSummary: Since רב יוסף's reading fails, the גמרא concludes that עולא's answer is the clear one: two תנאים reported רבי יהודה's view differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear: it is like עולא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב יוסף's reading and goes back to עולא's answer from Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said the משנה and the ברייתא come from two different תנאים who quoted רבי יהודה differently. Every attempt to make the two sources say the same thing has failed so far, so this answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear (a formula that drops the other attempts and confirms one answer)
As עולא said

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear: as Ulla (said).
phrases.notes: Back to the answer in Step 7

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא, כִּדְעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion after rejecting רב יוסף
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה and ברייתא reflect two versions of רבי יהודה's opinion, as עולא said

steps.title: רבה: until the time of slaughtering the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבה reads 'until פסח passes' as 'until the time of slaughtering the קרבן פסח passes.' So asking ends before פסח, while mentioning goes on into the first day, just as at the start of the season.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: What does 'until פסח passes' mean? Until the time of slaughtering the קרבן פסח passes. The beginning is like the end. Just as at the beginning one mentions rain even though one does not ask for it, so too at the end one mentions rain even though one does not ask for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה offers a new way to make the ברייתא fit the משנה. 'פסח' in the ברייתא means the קרבן פסח, slaughtered on the afternoon of י״ד ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, asking for rain stops on ערב פסח. Mentioning rain continues until the first day of פסח, as the משנה says. רבה supports this with a symmetry: at the start of the season we mention rain before we ask for it, so at the end we keep mentioning it after we stop asking.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering the קרבן פסח, done on the afternoon of the 14th of ניסן
Its end is like its beginning
Mentions rain (in the praise 'משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם')

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'הפסח' means the קרבן פסח (the offering), not the holiday. That is the whole point of רבה's reading.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
What is 'until Pesach passes'?
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא

phrases.english: Until the time of slaughtering the Pesach offering passes.
phrases.notes: Afternoon of י״ד ניסן

phrases.english: And its end is like its beginning:
Just as at its beginning one mentions (rain)
even though one does not request it,
so too at its end one mentions (rain)
even though one does not request it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר: מַאי עַד שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹר הַפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the גמרא went back to עולא, רבה tries a new way to make the sources agree
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads a word in the ברייתא ('פסח' = the קרבן פסח)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Until פסח passes' means through the holiday of פסח, which contradicts the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: Asking ends at the slaughter time on ערב פסח, and mentioning continues into the first day, mirroring the start of the season

steps.title: אביי: mentioning at the end leads to nothing
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבה's symmetry. Mentioning rain at the beginning prepares the way for asking. At the end there is no asking left to prepare for.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: It makes sense that at the beginning one mentions rain, because mentioning also prepares the way for asking. But at the end, what asking is there to prepare for?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה's idea that the end of the season mirrors the beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mentioning rain before asking acts like a warm-up, winning favor before the actual request. That reason only works when a request is coming. At the end of the season the asking has already stopped, so mentioning rain serves no purpose, and the two ends are not the same.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that... (grants one side before attacking the other)
Winning favor in advance of a request
Mentioning rain

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
It makes sense that at the beginning one mentions,
since mentioning is also a winning-of-favor for the request,
phrases.notes: It prepares for the coming request

phrases.english: but at the end,
what winning-of-favor for a request is there?
phrases.notes: There is no request left

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: בִּשְׁלָמָא תְּחִילָּתוֹ מַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's symmetry argument from Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the end of the season mirrors the beginning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mentioning only makes sense as a lead-in to asking, so it cannot continue after asking has ended

steps.title: Again, it must be like עולא
steps.stepSummary: With רבה's reading rejected too, the גמרא again concludes that עולא's answer is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear: it is like עולא.
steps.whatsHappening: For the second time, the גמרא drops an attempt to make the sources agree and goes back to עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רב יוסף and רבה tried to make the ברייתא match the משנה, and both failed. That leaves עולא's position: two תנאים disagree about what רבי יהודה held.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא ('until פסח passes') and the משנה (stop mentioning on the first day of פסח) cannot be made to agree. As עולא said, they are two different reports of רבי יהודה's opinion.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear: as Ulla (said).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא כִּדְעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion after rejecting רבה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עולא's answer of two differing תנאים stands

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said that רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the practical ruling: which opinion do we follow?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's view in the משנה is that the last prayer leader of the last day of סוכות mentions rain, while the first does not. רבי יוחנן rules this way. This sets up רבי זירא's challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows...
The תנא whose view on when to start mentioning rain is being ruled on

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for when to start mentioning rain, so the next challenge tests whether רבי יוחנן really said it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from settling the sources to the practical ruling

steps.title: רבי זירא: but רבי אלעזר ruled like רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא questions whether רבי יוחנן really said this. A later משנה says rain is asked for from the 3rd of מרחשון, רבן גמליאל says from the 7th, and רבי אלעזר ruled like רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי אסי: Did רבי יוחנן really say that? But we learned in a משנה: On the 3rd of מרחשון we ask for rain. רבן גמליאל says: on the 7th of it. And רבי אלעזר said: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges the ruling reported in Step 16 by quoting another משנה and a ruling of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר was רבי יוחנן's main student, so his ruling is assumed to reflect רבי יוחנן's view. Ruling like רבי יהודה means rain starts on שמיני עצרת, but ruling like רבן גמליאל means rain is not asked for until the 7th of מרחשון. The challenge assumes mentioning and asking start together, so the two rulings give conflicting start dates.

keyTerms.meaning: But did he really say...? (doubts a reported statement)
But didn't we learn in a משנה...?
The month after תשרי
The תנא who delays asking for rain until the 7th of מרחשון

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not saying that רבי אלעזר disagrees with רבי יוחנן. His point is that רבי אלעזר, as רבי יוחנן's student, reflects רבי יוחנן's view, and that view seems to conflict with ruling like רבי יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Asi:
And did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But didn't we learn in a mishnah:
phrases.notes: משנה on 6a

phrases.english: On the third of Marcheshvan we request rain,
Rabban Gamliel says: on the seventh of it.
And Rabbi Elazar said:
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן's main student

phrases.english: The halacha follows Rabban Gamliel!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבי יוחנן really gave the ruling quoted in Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's school (through רבי אלעזר) rules like רבן גמליאל, who starts on the 7th of מרחשון, while ruling like רבי יהודה starts on שמיני עצרת. If asking and mentioning begin together, these two rulings are incompatible.

steps.title: Two different people can disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי answers רבי זירא: you cannot set one sage's view against another sage's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you setting one man against another man?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי gives his first answer to רבי זירא's challenge. רבי אלעזר is a different person from רבי יוחנן, so they are allowed to disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's challenge assumed that a student's ruling shows what his teacher holds. רבי אסי rejects that assumption. רבי אלעזר may have his own opinion, so there is no real contradiction inside רבי יוחנן's words.

keyTerms.meaning: one man against another man
are you throwing (raising a contradiction)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: גַּבְרָא אַגַּבְרָא קָא רָמֵית?!
phrases.english: He (רבי אסי) said to him: Are you setting one man against another man?!
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן are two different sages, so they can hold different views.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבְרָא אַגַּבְרָא קָא רָמֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge from step 17
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's ruling must reflect what רבי יוחנן holds
steps.terutzMaskana: Two separate sages may simply disagree

steps.title: One ruling is about asking, the other about mentioning
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: רבי אלעזר's ruling is about asking for rain, and רבי יוחנן's is about mentioning rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say instead: there is no difficulty. Here it is about asking, and there it is about mentioning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי offers another way out, so there is no need to say the two sages disagree. Each ruling talks about a different prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר follows רבן גמליאל only for asking for rain, which starts on the 7th of מרחשון. רבי יוחנן follows רבי יהודה only for mentioning rain, which starts at שמיני עצרת. Since they speak about two different things, they do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: if you wish, say (introduces another answer)
to ask (the request for rain, 'ותן טל ומטר')
to mention (praising ה׳ as the One who brings rain, 'משיב הרוח')

steps.confusionAlert: 'Mentioning' (הזכרה) and 'asking' (שאלה) are two different things. Mentioning is praising ה׳ who brings rain. Asking is actually requesting rain.

phrases.english: If you wish, say: it is not difficult:
here it is about asking, there it is about mentioning.
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר (7th of מרחשון) = asking; רבי יוחנן (שמיני עצרת) = mentioning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן לִשְׁאוֹל, כָּאן לְהַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer that keeps רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר in agreement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings are about the same prayer
steps.terutzMaskana: One ruling is about asking and the other about mentioning, so they do not clash

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן said asking and mentioning go together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the split: רבי יוחנן himself said that whenever one asks, one mentions.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יוחנן say: At the time when one asks, one mentions!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 19. It quotes רבי יוחנן linking asking and mentioning together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If asking and mentioning always happen at the same time, they cannot start on different dates. So you cannot split them to explain away the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't he say (introduces a challenge from a known statement)
where one asks, one mentions

phrases.english: But didn't רבי יוחנן say:
At the time when one asks, one mentions!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁשּׁוֹאֵל מַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the asking/mentioning split from step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רבי יוחנן's ruling is only about mentioning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן ties asking and mentioning together, so they cannot have different start dates

steps.title: That rule was said only about stopping
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן linked asking and mentioning only for when we stop, not for when we start.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was said about stopping.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the split. It limits רבי יוחנן's statement to the end of the rainy season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the end of the season we stop asking and mentioning on the same day. At the beginning, the two can still start on different days. So the split from step 19 survives for now.

keyTerms.meaning: stopping (ending the rain prayers)
it was said

phrases.english: That was said with regard to stopping.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא לְהַפְסָקָה אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Asking and mentioning are linked both at the start and at the end
steps.terutzMaskana: They are linked only at the end, when we stop

steps.title: רבי יוחנן said they are linked at the start too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another statement of רבי יוחנן that clearly links asking and mentioning at the start as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יוחנן say: Once he begins to mention, he begins to ask; once he stops asking, he stops mentioning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back with a more explicit quote. This one talks about starting too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This statement says that asking and mentioning start together and stop together. So the asking/mentioning split cannot work, and the answer from step 19 falls.

keyTerms.meaning: began
stopped

phrases.english: But didn't רבי יוחנן say:
once he began to mention, he begins to ask;
once he stopped asking, he stops mentioning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הִתְחִיל לְהַזְכִּיר מַתְחִיל לִשְׁאוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 21 and brings down the split of step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the link applies only to stopping
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן explicitly links them at the start as well

steps.title: One ruling is for בבל, the other for ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: A new answer: רבי אלעזר's ruling (7th of מרחשון) is for us in בבל, and רבי יוחנן's ruling is for them in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is no difficulty: this one is for us, and that one is for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The asking/mentioning split has failed, so the גמרא tries a new answer. The two rulings apply in different places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both rulings are about the same prayer, but in different countries. רבי אלעזר speaks for בבל. רבי יוחנן (following רבי יהודה) speaks for ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (drops the earlier answer)
this is for us (בבל), that is for them (ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
this is for us, that is for them.
phrases.notes: 'Us' = בבל (רבי אלעזר); 'them' = ארץ ישראל (רבי יוחנן).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא לַן, הָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected asking/mentioning answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings apply in the same place
steps.terutzMaskana: בבל asks later; ארץ ישראל asks right after the holiday

steps.title: But ארץ ישראל has pilgrims to worry about
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: בבל waits because of fruit still in the fields, but ארץ ישראל also has a reason to wait, because pilgrims are traveling home.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about us? That we have fruit in the field. They too have pilgrims!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the בבל/ארץ ישראל answer. ארץ ישראל seems to need a delay too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בבל delays the request because rain would damage the crops still in the fields. But ארץ ישראל also has a reason to delay. Rain would make it hard for the pilgrims going home after סוכות, which is רבן גמליאל's reason for the 7th of מרחשון. So why should ארץ ישראל ask right away?

keyTerms.meaning: what is different
fruit (produce) still in the field
pilgrims who came up to ירושלים for the holiday

phrases.english: What is different about us?
That we have fruit in the field.

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידְהוּ נָמֵי אִית לְהוּ עוֹלֵי רְגָלִים!
phrases.english: They too have pilgrims!
phrases.notes: The pilgrims need dry roads to travel home after סוכות.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא לְדִידַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the בבל/ארץ ישראל answer of step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ארץ ישראל asks right after סוכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ארץ ישראל has its own reason to delay, the pilgrims, so it should also wait

steps.title: רבי יוחנן spoke about a time with no בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's ruling is for when the בית המקדש is not standing, when there are no pilgrims.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוחנן said this, it was for the time when the בית המקדש is not standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא removes the pilgrim problem. רבי יוחנן was talking about a time with no pilgrims.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a בית המקדש, nobody makes the pilgrimage. So nobody needs dry roads, and ארץ ישראל can ask for rain right after the holiday.

keyTerms.meaning: when he said
when the בית המקדש is not standing

phrases.english: When רבי יוחנן said it,
it was for the time when the בית המקדש is not standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pilgrim challenge of step 24
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's ruling applies even when there are pilgrims
steps.terutzMaskana: It applies only when there is no בית המקדש, so there are no pilgrims

steps.title: Both rulings are for ארץ ישראל, in different eras
steps.stepSummary: Building on the last answer, the גמרא concludes that both rulings are for ארץ ישראל. The 7th of מרחשון applies when the בית המקדש stands, and right after the holiday applies when it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, both are for them, and there is no difficulty. Here it is when the בית המקדש is standing; there it is when the בית המקדש is not standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the בבל/ארץ ישראל split and gives a cleaner final answer. Both rulings are about ארץ ישראל, just in different eras.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the time of the בית המקדש is the key factor, there is no need to bring in בבל at all. רבי אלעזר (like רבן גמליאל, the 7th of מרחשון) speaks about the era of the בית המקדש, when there were pilgrims. רבי יוחנן (like רבי יהודה) speaks about our era. So רבי יוחנן's ruling stands without contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: now that you have arrived at this (idea)
both this and that

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer: in ארץ ישראל, when the בית המקדש stood, they waited until the 7th of מרחשון so the pilgrims could get home. Without the בית המקדש, they ask right after סוכות. So רבי יוחנן (like רבי יהודה) and רבי אלעזר (like רבן גמליאל) do not contradict each other.
steps.whyThisMatters: The start date for asking for rain depends on the reason behind it, the pilgrims. When the reason is gone, the delay is gone.

phrases.english: Now that you have arrived at this,
both this and that are for them (ארץ ישראל), and it is not difficult:
here, when the בית המקדש is standing,
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר / רבן גמליאל: wait until the 7th of מרחשון.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים.
phrases.english: there, when the בית המקדש is not standing.
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן / רבי יהודה: ask right away.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי, הָא וְהָא לְדִידְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses step 25's idea to replace the בבל/ארץ ישראל split with a cleaner answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both rulings are for ארץ ישראל: the 7th of מרחשון when the בית המקדש stands, and right after סוכות when it does not.

steps.title: What do we do with two days of יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how people in בבל, who keep two days of יום טוב, should start mentioning rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we, who have two days of יום טוב, what do we do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new practical question. It is setting up the answers of רב and שמואל that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We start mentioning rain on שמיני עצרת. Outside ארץ ישראל, we keep two days because we are not sure of the exact date. So the first day might really be the seventh day of סוכות, and the second day might be the real שמיני עצרת. The question is when to begin mentioning rain.

keyTerms.meaning: We (the people in בבל)
Two days of יום טוב, kept because of a calendar doubt
How do we act? / What do we do?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about whether to ask for rain in שמונה עשרה. It is only about when to start mentioning rain (משיב הרוח) in the second ברכה.

phrases.english: And we, who have two days [of יום טוב],
how do we act?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנַן דְּאִית לַן תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי הֵיכִי עָבְדִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ארץ ישראל to the practice in בבל, where two days of יום טוב create a doubt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: On which prayer do people with two days of יום טוב begin mentioning rain?

steps.title: רב's schedule: start, stop, then start again
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that you start at מוסף of the first day and stop at מנחה, ערבית and שחרית. Then you start again at מוסף of the second day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: You start mentioning rain at מוסף. You stop at מנחה, ערבית and שחרית. Then you go back to it at מוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question by covering both possibilities. He gives a schedule that switches back and forth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At מוסף of the first day, רב treats the day as possibly being שמיני עצרת, so you mention rain. From מנחה on, he treats the first day as possibly the seventh day of סוכות, so you stop. At מוסף of the second day, which may be the real שמיני עצרת, you start again for good.

keyTerms.meaning: Begins (mentioning rain)
The מוסף prayer
Stops
Goes back / resumes

phrases.english: Rav said:
One begins at the additional prayer (Musaf),
and stops at the afternoon, evening and morning prayers,
and resumes at the additional prayer (of the second day).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מַתְחִיל בְּמוּסָפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Start at מוסף of day one, stop from מנחה through שחרית of day two, and resume at מוסף of day two.

steps.title: שמואל objects: you made it holy, now you make it ordinary?
steps.stepSummary: שמואל sends a message to רב. Once you treated the first day as holy שמיני עצרת at מוסף, how can you treat it as ordinary at מנחה?
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to them: Go and tell אבא (רב): After you made it holy, will you now make it ordinary?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל attacks רב's schedule. He says it contradicts itself on the very same day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At מוסף, רב treated the first day as שמיני עצרת by mentioning rain. At מנחה of that same day, he stopped, as if the day were the seventh day of סוכות. To שמואל, that is like taking back the day's holiness, and you cannot flip within one day.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out and tell him
Abba, רב's personal name
Holy (treated as the holiday)
Ordinary, not holy

steps.confusionAlert: "אבא" here does not mean "father." It is רב's own name (אבא אריכא).

phrases.english: Shmuel said to them,
Go out and tell Abba (Rav):
After you have made it holy,
will you make it ordinary?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחַר שֶׁעֲשִׂיתוֹ קוֹדֶשׁ תַּעֲשֵׂהוּ חוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's answer from step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling to stop at מנחה of the first day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mentioning rain at מוסף treats the day as שמיני עצרת. Stopping at מנחה of the same day treats it as ordinary, which contradicts what you just did.

steps.title: שמואל's schedule: keep going through מנחה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that you start at מוסף and also say it at מנחה. You stop at ערבית and שחרית, then start again at מוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, שמואל said: You start mentioning rain at מוסף and at מנחה. You stop at ערבית and שחרית. Then you go back and start again at מוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: Since he rejected רב's schedule, שמואל gives his own answer to the question of step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only change from רב is מנחה of the first day. שמואל keeps mentioning rain at מנחה so the first day is not reversed partway through, which answers his own objection. He stops only at ערבית and שחרית, which belong to the next day, and resumes at מוסף of the second day.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the earlier view and replacing it)
The afternoon prayer
The evening and morning prayers

steps.whatToRemember: רב: start at מוסף, stop at מנחה, ערבית and שחרית, resume at מוסף of day two. שמואל: start at מוסף and keep it at מנחה, stop only at ערבית and שחרית, resume at מוסף of day two. They argue only about מנחה of the first day.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume שמואל stops at מנחה like רב. The text says 'מתחיל במוספין ובמנחה', so he keeps mentioning rain at מנחה of the first day and stops only at ערבית and שחרית.

phrases.english: Rather, Shmuel said:
One begins at Musaf and [continues] at Minchah,
and stops at the evening and morning prayers,
and goes back and begins again at Musaf.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מַתְחִיל בְּמוּסָפִין וּבְמִנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב's answer with a schedule that avoids the objection of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Start at מוסף and continue at מנחה of day one, stop at ערבית and שחרית, and resume at מוסף of day two.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea about days of doubt: once you treat a day one way, you should not reverse yourself within that same day.
